newsitem.title: TURKEY: Netanyahu happy with Turkish Islamist-led govt.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu happy with Turkish Islamist-led govt.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in comments published on Thursday he was happy with Turkey's Islamist-led government which had not turned out to be as radical as feared.
"Contrary to all our fears and concerns, today we are very pleased with Mr Erbakan's government," the Milliyet daily quoted Netanyahu as saying in an interview.
Before coming to power last June, Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had threatened to annul a military accord between Turkey and Israel that drew the wrath of Arab countries and Iran.

But Erbakan, under pressure from Turkey's secularist military, has since done nothing to scrap the agreement. Israeli air force planes last year took part in training flights over Turkey as part of the military deal.

Netanyahu said he had invited Erbakan to Israel almost six months ago but had not yet received a reply. Erbakan's Welfare Party is the senior partner in a coalition with a pro-Western party headed by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.
The Israeli leader called for closer business ties with NATO member Turkey, a Moslem but officially secular state.
"Come and let us make joint investments together. This is one of the most important reasons for my desire for dialogue with Mr Erbakan's government," he said.
Netanyahu said there could be a role for Turkey in the Middle East peace process as it is a Moslem country which has good relations with both Israel and Arab countries.
Israel wanted Turks to take part in the international force of observers in the West Bank town of Hebron, he said.
